   Guide to City Council Proceedings

Meetings of the City Council are held the first and third Tuesday of each month at 9:00 a.m. and are
conducted in accordance with Rosenberg's Rules of Order (Vernon Municipal Code Section 2.04.020).

Copies of all agenda items and back-up materials are available for review in the City Clerk Department,
Vernon City Hall, 4305 Santa Fe Avenue, Vernon, California, and are available for public inspection
during regular business hours, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Agenda reports may be
reviewed on the City's website at www.cityofvernonca.gov or copies may be purchased for $0.20 per
page.

Disability-related services are available to enable persons with a disability to participate in this
meeting, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). In compliance with ADA, if you need
special assistance, please contact the City Clerk department at CityClerk@cityofvernonca.gov or (323)
583-8811 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to assure arrangements can be made.

The general Public Comment portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which
are not listed on the agenda but are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Consent
Calendar and Closed Session. The City Council cannot take action on any item that is not on the
agenda, but matters raised under Public Comment may be referred to staff or scheduled on a future
agenda. Public Comment for Public Hearings and New Business items will be heard during the
consideration of the item. Comments are limited to three minutes per speaker unless a different time limit
is announced. Speaker slips are available at the entrance to the Council Chamber.

Public Hearings are legally noticed hearings. For hearings involving zoning matters, the applicant and
appellant will be given 15 minutes to present their position to the City Council. Time may be set aside for
rebuttal. All other testimony shall follow the rules as set for under Public Comment. If you challenge any
City action in court, you may be limited to raising only those issues you or someone else raised during
the public hearing, or in written correspondence delivered to the City Clerk at or prior to the public
hearing.

Consent Calendar items may be approved by a single motion. If a Council Member or the public wishes
to discuss an item, it may be removed from the calendar for individual consideration. Council Members
may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the
motion to adopt the Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up
following action on the Consent Calendar. Public speakers shall follow the guidelines as set forth under
Public Comment.

New Business items are matters appearing before the Council for the first time for formal action. Those
wishing to address the Council on New Business items shall follow the guidelines for Public Comment.

Closed Session allows the Council to discuss specific matters pursuant to the Brown Act, Government
Code Section 54956.9. Based on the advice of the City Attorney, discussion of these matters in open
session would prejudice the position of the City. The public can comment on Closed Session matters
during the general Public Comment portion of the meeting. Following Closed Session, the City Attorney
will provide an oral report on any reportable matters discussed and actions taken. At the conclusion of
Closed Session, the Council may continue any item listed on the Closed Session agenda to the Open
Session agenda for discussion or to take formal action as it deems appropriate.

Meeting Date:  July 21, 2026
From:  Robert Sousa, Chief of Police
Department:  Police
Submitted by:  Nicholas Perez, Captain

Subject
Swearing-In Ceremony for New Police Officer

Recommendation
Administer the Oath of Office to Police Officer Sergio De La Torre Jr.

Background
The City Council typically hosts a public swearing-in ceremony when new Police Officers are
hired. During the past few months, the Police Department (PD) has vacated positions due to the
separation of employees during their probationary period. The PD has filled the vacancies as
leaving these positions vacant would negatively impact the necessary patrol deployment and
would increase overtime costs to cover staff shortages.

To fill the vacancies, PD, with assistance from the Human Resources Department, conducted
the necessary recruitment processes. Based on a review of the qualifications of each eligible
candidate and the completion of an extensive background investigation, Sergio De La Torre Jr.
was selected as the best-qualified candidate to fill a vacant Police Officer position.

Officer De La Torre has been invited to attend the July 21st Council Meeting with his family for a
public swearing-in and badge-pinning ceremony.

Strategic Plan Goals
Goal 1: Strengthen City Credibility and Partnerships

Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Principal Management Analyst

Subject
Proclamation Recognizing Retiring Employee – Claudia Arellano

Recommendation
Acknowledge and present a proclamation to retiring employee Claudia Arellano, Utilities Program
Analyst, in recognition of her dedicated service to the City of Vernon.

Background
Historically, the City Council has issued proclamations honoring retiring City employees. Claudia
Arellano, Utilities Program Analyst, is retiring from the City of Vernon on August 3, 2026, after
providing over thirty-four (34) years of service to the City. Claudia was hired with the City of
Vernon effective November 4, 1991.

Claudia began her career with the City as a Utility Clerk on November 4, 1991. She was
reclassified to Secretary on July 1, 1995, and then to Department Secretary on September 9,
2001. Following this, she was promoted to Assistant to the Director of Community Services.
Utilizing her extensive knowledge, she was reclassified to Project Engineer on February 1, 2011,
and then to Stormwater Special Projects Analyst on April 20, 2014. Claudia was promoted to
Utilities Program Analyst on December 1, 2020, concluding her distinguished career with the
City.

During her 34-year tenure, Ms. Arellano held seven positions across three city departments: City
Administration, Public Works, and Public Utilities. Her historical knowledge of city operations,
diverse work experience, and “can-do " attitude made her an integral resource for city staff.

Throughout her career, Claudia played a key role in major initiatives, including securing external
grant funding to plant 200 trees, achieving the City's first Tree City USA designation, and
supporting regional collaboration on environmental stormwater initiatives.

Within the Public Utilities Department, she played a key role in managing critical Natural Gas
Division programs, and leading the Division through its first-ever comprehensive pipeline safety
regulatory audit, resulting in a perfect inspection with zero findings and zero recommendations—
an exceptional outcome reflecting her strong knowledge of pipeline safety regulations, natural
gas operations, and her extraordinary preparation and attention to detail.

During her distinguished career with the City of Vernon, Claudia Arellano earned the deepest
respect of her colleagues, recognized for her professionalism, kindness, and unwavering
commitment to serving the public and the Vernon business community. Claudia Arellano was
hired on November 4, 1991, and meets the eligibility requirements under CalPERS to retire from
the City effective August 3, 2026.

  A PROCLAMATION OF THE MAYOR AND THE CITY COUNCIL
  COMMENDING CLAUDIA ARELLAN~ FOR HER MANY YEARS OF
  SERVICE TO THE CITY OF VERNON
  WHEREAS, Claudia Arellano has been a dedicated employee of the City of Vernon for over thirty-
four years and faithfully performed her duties as a public servant since August 3, 1991; and

  WHEREAS, Claudia meets the eligibility requirements under CaIPERS to retire from the City of Vernon
effective August 3, 2026, as a Utilities Program Analyst; and

  WHEREAS, during her employment with the City of Vernon, Claudia held various positions in City
Administration, Public Works, and Public Utilities Department, including Utility Clerk, Secretary, Department
Secretary, Assistant to the Director of Community Services, Project Engineer, Stormwater Special Projects
Analyst, and Utilities Program Analyst; and

  WHEREAS, Claudia continually expanded her knowledge and expertise throughout her career,
supporting several departments through extensive hands-on experience, technical training, and
professional certifications, including a certification in Stormwater Inspection; and

  WHEREAS, during her three decades of service, Claudia played a critical role in providing support
for: City Administration and the City's risk management program; Public Works' tree canopy and
stormwater programs; Public Utilities Engineering Division's pole attachments program; and led regulatory
compliance while supporting budget and administrative functions in the Utility's Natural Gas Division; and

  WHEREAS, while in the Public Works Department, Claudia successfully secured external funding to
advance the City's efforts to grow its tree canopy and support its commitment to urban forestry including
obtaining a Cal Fire Cool Parks Program grant to plant more than 200 trees throughout the City, leading
the City's successful application for its first-ever Tree City USA designation in 2019, and collaborating with
neighboring jurisdictions to secure grant funding for regional stormwater improvement projects; and

  WHEREAS, as a valued member of the Public Utilities Natural Gas Division, Claudia was instrumental
in implementing and managing key initiatives, including oversight of the pipeline safety public awareness
program and federal regulatory reporting to the Pipeline Hazardous Materials Safety Administration and
the California Public Utilities Commission; and

  WHEREAS, Claudia led the Public Utilities Natural Gas Division through its first-ever comprehensive
pipeline safety regulatory audit, resulting in a perfect inspection with zero findings and zero
recommendations—an exceptional outcome reflecting her strong knowledge of pipeline safety
regulations, natural gas operations, and her extraordinary preparation and attention to detail; and

  WHEREAS, Claudia consistently demonstrates an exemplary attitude and inspires excellence from
others through her daily interactions with her colleagues, her unwavering positivity, and collaborative spirit;
all of which make Claudia an integral part of the City's success in serving its customers, and will have a
lasting impact on the City; and

  WHEREAS, we congratulate and express our appreciation to Claudia for her commendable service
to the City of Vernon and wish Claudia good health upon her retirement and for continued success in life's
pursuits.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE MAYOR AND THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF VERNON, ON BEHALF OF ITS
EMPLOYEES, RESIDENTS AND BUSINESSES HEREBY COMMEND AND THANK CLAUDIA ARELLANO FOR HER YEARS
OF SERVICE TO THE CITY. THIS PROCLAMATION IS BEING PRESENTED TO CLAUDIA ARELLANO BY THE
HONORABLE MAYOR MELISSA YBARRA FOR AND ON BEHALF OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF VERNON
THIS 21ST DAY OF JULY TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY-SIX.

  CITY OF VERNON

1.  Ratification of Proclamation of Local Emergency
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-034 ratifying the Chief Executive
  Officer’s proclamation of local emergency as a result of the threat to public health
  from the Palos Warehouse Fire.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra inquired what the City has learned and done to avoid similar
  incidents happening in the City.

  City Administrator Saeki stated that the lessons learned will continue to evolve as
  staff finds how these fires are efficiently extinguished and the smoke is mitigated,
  which could lead to code and design changes for future developments. City
  Administrator Saeki informed the City Council that staff had met to discuss how
  credible information will be communicated to community via several tools.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comment, there being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to Adopt Resolution No. 2026-034 ratifying the Chief Executive Officer’s
  proclamation of local emergency as a result of the threat to public health from the
  Palos Warehouse Fire. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0,
  Council Member Merlo was absent.

  Activity Report • City of Vernon

Incident Summary – May 2026
During May 2026, the County of Los Angeles Fire Department responded to nine outside fire
incidents and two hazardous-situation investigations.

Outside fires included trash, brush, and other small outdoor fires occurring at various locations
throughout the City of Vernon. Several incidents involved fires associated with unhoused
individuals, including one fire on Vernon Avenue that spread beneath an exterior stairwell and
resulted in charring to structural members, though no active structural fire extension was
found.

Other incidents involved rubbish fires along roadways, beneath a freeway bridge, and
adjacent to buildings, all of which were extinguished without reported injuries. One rubbish fire
was suspected to have been caused by a lithium-ion battery, and another trashcan fire was
extinguished by an automatic sprinkler system before fire personnel arrived.

The Department also responded to two hazardous-situation investigations: a propane bottle
explosion at a business, where no injuries were reported and the scene was secured, and an
investigation of an odor originating from a rail car. Following an inspection by BNSF Railway
and Department personnel, no hazardous materials were identified in the rail car.

   City Council Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  July 21, 2026
From:  Todd Dusenberry, General Manager of Public Utilities
Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Principal Management Analyst

Subject
Services Agreement with EN Engineering, LLC dba ENTRUST Solutions Group

Recommendation
A. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute a Services Agreement with EN
Engineering LLC, dba ENTRUST Solutions Group (EN Engineering), in substantially the same
form as submitted, for Natural Gas Operational and Compliance Support Services for a total
amount not-to-exceed $352,000, for a three-year term; and
B. Authorize a contingency amount of five percent (5%) or $17,600 in the event of unforeseen
services and expenses related to ongoing compliance support needs, staffing limitations, and the
new audit format implemented by the CPUC, and grant authority to the City Administrator to
approve and execute contract amendments up to the contingency amount, if necessary.

Background
The Natural Gas Division of Vernon Public Utilities was established in 2006 with a large
distribution system to serve the City's industrial and commercial sectors. VPU provides natural
gas service to approximately 125 industrial and commercial customers. The City's transmission
system became operational in 2005. Although Vernon is a small city with a natural gas utility
serving approximately 125 customers, VPU is one of the largest municipal gas providers by
volume in the United States.

VPU maximizes the operational efficiency of its natural gas system by utilizing fulltime employees
to manage day-to-day operations while retaining specialized consultants to provide technical
expertise for periodic or otherwise specialized requirements. This strategy maintains efficiencies,
keeps internal costs competitive, and ensures that expertise and experience are available and
utilized as needed.

The pipeline industry continues to face increased scrutiny by regulators, the media, and the
public. In 2018, the Pipeline Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) outsourced
the California Pipeline Safety Audits to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC). More
recently, VPU was notified to expect annual audits. This represents a dramatic increase, as
PHMSA audits were previously conducted every two to three years. In addition, the CPUC audits
are performed by a team of technical experts, as opposed to PHMSA audits, which are performed
by a single inspector. Several factors necessitate continued compliance support services,
including increased audit scrutiny, the need to develop and implement feedback from CPUC
inspectors in recent years, and compliance with new regulations.

The City has utilized the services of EN Engineering, LLC dba ENTRUST Solutions Group (EN
Engineering) for natural gas operational and compliance support services. On June 20, 2023,
the City Council approved a three-year Services Agreement with EN Engineering to provide
natural gas operational and compliance support services. That agreement expired on June 30,
2026. As per Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) 3.32.080, on May 7, 2026, staff issued a Request
for .Proposals (RFP) to seek proposals from consultants to continue providing natural gas
operational
  .  and compliance support services. The RFP was advertised on the City's Planet Bids
  Item 8  Page 1 of 176
 platform. The RFP identified the following compliance areas: Audit Support, Regulatory
Compliance Support, Programs Documents and Procedure, Subject Matter Expertise in the
documentation and development of processes, Quarterly Compliance and Record Reviews,
General Compliance Support, and Training Resources.

Proposal packages were received from two firms by the May 20, 2026 deadline. A qualified panel
of City staff from multiple departments thoroughly examined the proposals based on professional
qualifications (45%), demonstrated competence (45%), and responsiveness to the RFP (10%).
Based on the evaluation process, the proposal submitted by EN Engineering demonstrated the
strongest combination of expertise and a comprehensive approach that was best suited to fulfill
the scope of services that were outlined in the RFP. The proposal submitted by EN Engineering
received the highest score following the evaluation process and was therefore deemed the most
qualified.

EN Engineering has significant experience in providing natural gas operational and compliance
support services to VPU, including successfully assisted VPU in receiving the first known audit
that concluded with no findings.

VPU staff recommends that the City Council approve a Services Agreement with EN Engineering
for a total amount not-to-exceed $352,000 to provide natural gas operational and compliance
support services. Additionally, staff recommends a contingency amount of five percent (5%) or
$17,600, in the event of unforeseen services and expenses related to ongoing compliance
support needs, staffing limitations, and the new audit format implemented by the CPUC, for a
combined total not to exceed $369,600. Pursuant to VMC Section 3.32.030(A), City Council
approval is required for the proposed agreement, as the total value of the contract exceeds
$100,000.

The proposed Services Agreement has been reviewed and approved as to form by the City
Attorney's Office.

Strategic Plan Goals

Fiscal Impact
The fiscal impact is not-to-exceed $369,600. Sufficient funds are available in the Electric Fund,
Administration, Professional Services – Technical, Account No. 055-050-580-529225 for the
current fiscal year and will be budgeted in subsequent years.

  INTRODUCTION
 ENTRUST is pleased to provide this proposal for compliance support services for the City
 of Vernon’s Public Utilities (VPU) Natural Gas utilities division. ENTRUST believes our
 experience and expertise is a perfect fit for the City of Vernon to ensure continued
 compliance with state and federal regulations for pipeline safety.

 ENTRUST’s proposal is based off the request for proposal (RFP) from the City of Vernon
 to provide the following services:

  GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK
 The City of Vernon provides natural gas to approximately 125 commercial and industrial
 customers and has the infrastructure to serve approximately 900 customers within the City’s
 service area. Gas is delivered to the City at two receiving stations. The City's transmission system
 became operational in 2005 and is a designated high-consequence area. It is comprised of 7
 miles of 10-inch steel main. The City’s distribution system became operational in 2006 and
 consists of approximately 45 miles of 6-inch Polyethylene (PE) pipe. The City of Vernon pipeline
 system is subject to the compliance requirements of Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)
 Parts 190, 191, 192, and 199.

 ENTRUST has extensive experience in performing regulatory compliance services for
 natural gas and hazardous liquid pipeline operators. ENTRUST is uniquely positioned
 with multiple staff members who are previous inspectors with the Pipeline and Hazardous
 Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) and have a strong background in the
 interpretation and application of code requirements.

 WORK PLAN
 ENTRUST proposes the following sample project work plan similar to those employed by
 ENTRUST when performing work for other utility operators across the country.

 Task 1 – Audit Support

 ENTRUST will provide compliance support for one (1) state or federal audit per calendar
 year based on PHMSA Integrated Inspection protocols. This will include the following:

  1. Three (3) days of off-site preparation time.
  2. One (1) 40-hour week of on-site support during the live audit execution.

 ENTRUST’s support will ensure baseline audit readiness. Any additional audits or support
 beyond these designated hourly limits will be provided on a time and materials (T&M)
 basis. Post-audit remediation support is excluded from this scope and will be proposed
 separately upon review of actual audit findings.

 Deliverables will include a pre-audit gap analysis report outlining identified risks and
 recommended mitigation actions, followed by both off-site and on-site audit execution
 support within the designated hourly limits.

 Task 2 – Ongoing Review and Management of Pipeline Compliance Programs
 ENTRUST will support VPU gas division personnel in performance of an annual review
 of the VPU Gas Pipeline compliance programs. This will include the following:
  1. Operations and Maintenance Manual & associated procedures
  2. Operator Qualification Manual
  3. Damage Prevention Plan

Subject
Extending State of Local Emergency

Recommendation
Renew Resolution No. 2026-034, ratifying Emergency Proclamation No. 2026-001, a
proclamation of local emergency due to the Palos Warehouse Fire.

Background
On June 17, 2026, a structural fire ignited in a large cold storage warehouse in the Boyle Heights
neighborhood in the City of Los Angeles (Palos Warehouse Fire). Located just north of City of
Vernon boundaries, the Palos Warehouse Fire impacted air quality in the City and throughout
the region prompting the South Coast Air Quality Management District (South Coast AQMD) to
issue a Particle Pollution Advisory for several days following the fire. Due to the significant
impacts to the community, on June 20, 2026, Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a State of
Emergency to exist in Los Angeles County due to the Palos Warehouse Fire (Attachment 2).

Also effective on June 20, 2026, Mayor Melissa Ybarra, acting as the Chief Executive Officer of
the Vernon Disaster Council, issued a Proclamation of Local Emergency declaring the existence
of a local state of emergency in the City of Vernon due to the Palos Warehouse Fire. Pursuant
to Government Code Section 8630 and Vernon Municipal Code Section 2.36.050(B)(1), within
seven (7) days of Emergency Proclamation No. 2026-001 being issued, on June 23, 2026, the
City Council adopted Resolution No. 2026-034 ratifying the Chief Executive Officer’s
proclamation of local emergency (Attachment 1). Pursuant to Government Code Section 8630,
the governing body shall review the need for continuing the local emergency at least once every
60 days until the governing body terminates the local emergency, and the termination shall occur
at the earliest possible date that conditions warrant. Accordingly, staff are providing information
regarding the current conditions in the areas near the fire.

Currently, the Palos Warehouse Fire continues to significantly impact the local community as
ongoing cleanup efforts, including the removal of approximately 85 million pounds of spoiled food
waste, are generating increased odors, dust from demolition work, debris removal and increased
truck traffic. The community has also expressed concern regarding an increased presence of
flies, vermin, and rodents. As a result, government agencies and community-based organizations
continue efforts to assist affected households by providing air purifiers, temporary relocation
assistance, food assistance, health screenings, masks, water, personal hygiene products, and
other emergency relief supplies. The ongoing odor issues reported by numerous community
complaints prompted the South Coast AQMD to issue a Notice of Violation (NOV) to the facility
operator (Lineage Logistics, LLC) on at least two separate occasions for violations of its public
nuisance rules.

Following the fire, the City received emergency funding requests from local non-profit community
organizations including Proyecto Pastoral and Labor Community Services that are actively
providing aid to residents affected by the Palos Warehouse Fire. Providing financial assistance

  WHEREAS on June 17, 2026, a structural fire ignited in a large cold storage

Angeles County (“Palos Warehouse Fire”); and

  WHEREAS the Palos Warehouse Fire involved a large commercial cold-
storage facility that contained refrigeration systems, rooftop solar-panel
infrastructure, and other industrial equipment; and

  WHEREAS during firefighting operations, emergency responders
encountered complex conditions, including hazardous materials such as
ammonia, requiring a specialized response and air monitoring, as well as
continued fire flare ups; and

  WHEREAS the Palos Warehouse Fire generated a substantial smoke plume
necessitating a shelter-in-place order, which has since been lifted, and smoke
and particle pollution advisories throughout neighboring communities; and

  WHEREAS the cold-storage warehouse rooftop solar infrastructure,
hazardous materials, and lithium-ion batteries on site, and approximately 85
million pounds of decaying food products contribute to an incident at the
warehouse beyond the mitigation capabilities of traditional firefighting
equipment and methods available to the City of Los Angeles and Los Angeles
County; and

  WHEREAS under the provisions of Government Code section 8558(b), I
find conditions of extreme peril to the safety of persons and property exist due
to the Palos Warehouse Fire in Los Angeles County; and

  WHEREAS under the provisions of Government Code section 8558(b), I
find the conditions caused by the Palos Warehouse Fire, by reason of their
magnitude, are or are likely to be beyond the control of the services,
personnel, equipment, and facilities of any single local government and
require the combined forces of a mutual aid region or regions to appropriately
respond; and

  WHEREAS under the provisions of Government Code section 8625(c), I
find that local authority is inadequate to cope with the magnitude of the
extreme peril posed by the Palos Warehouse Fire; and

  WHEREAS under the provisions of Government Code section 8571, I find
that strict compliance with various statutes and regulations specified in this
Proclamation would prevent, hinder, or delay the mitigation of the effects of
the Palos Warehouse Fire in the City of Los Angeles.

  NOW, THEREFORE, I, GAVIN NEWSOM, Governor of the State of California,
in accordance with the authority vested in me by the State Constitution and
statutes, including the California Emergency Services Act, and in particular,

Recommendation
Receive and file a report on the second-year renewal of Contract No. 20250416 with Granicus,
Inc. for a one-year term for agenda management software for an amount not-to-exceed

Background
The City utilizes the Granicus agenda management platform to support the preparation, review,
approval, publication, and archiving of City Council and other legislative meeting agendas and
supporting documents. The platform provided by Granicus, Inc. (Granicus) also provides meeting
management, video streaming, and integration with the City's Laserfiche records management
system.

On June 16, 2025, the City entered a one-year agreement for these services. This original
agreement with Granicus (Contract No. 20250416) included annual renewal terms and on June
23, 2026, with the authorization of the City Administrator, and following consultation with the City
Clerk, the Information Technology Division (IT) completed the second-year renewal to ensure
the continued operation of the software platform and uninterrupted support for City meeting
management functions. Granicus continues to serve as a critical digital platform that enables the
City to efficiently manage meeting agendas, legislative documents, agenda packet publication,
video streaming, and records management. Over the past year, the software has supported the
City's efforts to modernize government operations by improving workflow efficiency, enhancing
public transparency, and ensuring access to meeting information for both staff and the public.
Prior to the expiration of the renewal term, the City Clerk and IT will evaluate other potential
options for agenda management software.

Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) Section 3.32.110(B)(2), the City Administrator found
that continuing services with the existing provider was in the best interests of the City, as the
renewal serves to maintain operational continuity through established processes and workflows,
preserves the City's prior investment in the platform, and provides continued access to software
updates and enhancements. This report regarding the direct award of the contract without a

Subject
Report on Emergency Repair of Combustion Turbine Generator Approved by the City
Administrator

Recommendation
Receive and file a report on the emergency repair of Combustion Turbine Generator No. 1
performed by Siemens Energy, including ABB Support, and D2 Industrial Services, LLC, as
approved by the City Administrator pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section 3.32.250.

Background
On August 21, 2025, the Malburg Generating Station (MGS) experienced an unexpected outage
when the Siemens Combustion Turbine Generator No. 1 (CTG 1) unit tripped while operating at
a base load of 42.5 Megawatts (MW). The City Administrator and VPU Management were
immediately notified of the failure, and the emergency response process was implemented,
including notification to the City Administrator that CTG 1 expenditures for repair work and related
replacement parts would be considered as Emergency Purchases, pursuant to Section 3.32.250
of the Vernon Municipal Code (VMC).

The initial cause of the trip was identified as a generator overload, which occurred when a
permanent rotor segment was detached from the shaft, leading to damage in the exciter winding.
The exciter is a critical component of the generator system, and its failure rendered CTG 1
inoperable until repairs could be completed. With CTG 1 offline, the plant’s dispatch capacity
was significantly reduced, affecting its ability to meet load obligations, respond to grid demands,
as well as meeting Resource Adequacy (RA) requirements. To thoroughly inspect the unit,
immediate mobilization of multiple vendors was necessary to assess the situation, develop a
repair strategy, and provide support services to restore the unit to operation as quickly as
possible. VPU engaged multiple vendors including Siemens Energy, Inc. and D2 Industrial
Services LLC for the necessary repair work.

Siemens Energy, Inc.
Purchase Order (PO) No. 260321 was issued to Siemens Energy, Inc. (Siemens) with ABB as a
subcontractor for immediate repairs to CTG 1. The PO was for an amount of $188,820.37 and
covered the initial disassembly, diagnosis, repair strategy, and reassembly of the unit.

D2 Industrial Services LLC
Purchase Contract No. 20260096 with D2 Industrial Services, LLC (D2 Industrial) was initially
issued for $4,690. During the repair process, additional support was required, resulting in
increased expenses. Consequently, approval for a change order in the amount of $4,695 was
necessary raising the total for the Purchase Contract to $9,385.

Section 3.32.250 of the VMC states: “In case of an actual emergency which requires immediate
purchase of supplies, equipment, or services to address an immediate and unforeseen risk to
health,
  .  life, property or the environment, or for emergency work to restore or prevent an imminent
and. unforeseen failure of utility service, the City Administrator may secure, without competitive
  Item 11  Page 1 of 191
 bidding, at the lowest obtainable price, any supplies, equipment, or services regardless of the
amount of the expenditure.” The inspection and repair of the CTG 1 unit was deemed an
emergency, as the generator had become inoperable, leaving only one functional CTG to meet
MGS operating requirements and meet system reliability. Given the complexity of the repairs and
the urgent need for mobilization, the vendors required time to determine the total charges
incurred for the CTG 1 emergency repairs. VPU requested approval of the final amounts for the
emergency work once final invoices were received. Accordingly, on December 1, 2025, the City
Administrator approved the POs and payment to Siemens for a total amount of $188,820.37 and
Contract and related change order to D2 Industrial for a total amount of $9,385 for the emergency
repair work of CTG 1. The City Administrator’s approval was based on the immediate need to
minimize downtime and restore power plant operations, as well as to prevent an imminent failure
of utility service.

Emergency purchases approved by the City Administrator pursuant to VMC Section 3.32.250
require that a report detailing the circumstances of the emergency work be provided to the City
Council. It was recently identified by the Finance Department that the report related to the CTG
1 emergency repairs had not yet been provided to City Council. City Administration has since
made changes to its approval process to ensure that moving forward required reports are
provided timely.

Timeline to Implement Changes
Changes to the schedule for regular meetings of the City Council need to be made by Ordinance
pursuant to Chapter 3.10 of Article III of the Vernon City Charter. An Ordinance for this purpose
would require a first and second reading and become effective 30 days following adoption.
Should the City Council desire to make changes to its regular meeting schedule, at the earliest,
an Ordinance could be presented for consideration at the August 4, 2026 Council Meeting. If a
second reading and adoption occur at the subsequent meeting on August 18, 2026, the changes
would become effective as early as mid-September depending on Council direction.
